incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an elaborate AI-driven scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos using his image to promote fraudulent immigration services, including offers of US residency for $2,200. The scheme escalated dramatically over the past three months after Leal first noticed suspicious activity last October, with scammers directing victims through WhatsApp to send money via payment apps like Venmo and Zelle.

To combat the fraud, Leal hired an online anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically feature fake testimonials from supposed clients or false claims about immigration detention center services. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scheme. He warns immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to avoid anyone requesting immediate payment through digital payment platforms.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
A fake online article featuring ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler and Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock in a heated interview about an unlicensed cryptocurrency platform called Boulder Sparhaven never actually occurred. This fabricated story exemplifies a growing type of scam that uses artificial intelligence and deepfake technology to create convincing but false investment opportunities. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission reports that such schemes are becoming increasingly sophisticated and prevalent online.

ASIC's new research reveals alarming growth in investment scams, with the regulator taking down 19,400 scams last year, representing a 182 percent increase. Phishing scams jumped 279 percent, while fake investment platforms surged 151 percent. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, politician Pauline Hanson, businessman Dick Smith, and billionaire Gina Rinehart are among the most commonly impersonated public figures. Scammers build elaborate webs of deception using fake news articles, positive reviews, and websites before requesting personal details. ASIC advises consumers to verify Australian Financial Services licence numbers through official registers before investing and to distrust opportunities that seem too good to be true.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A class-action lawsuit filed by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco accuses Oura, the smart ring company, of false advertising regarding its sleep tracking capabilities. The suit alleges that Oura's rings, which cost $300 and up, cannot accurately measure sleep stages as claimed despite marketing statements like "95% Sleep Staging Accuracy compared to clinical sleep lab." The lawsuit contends that Oura's devices rely on unreliable AI-generated estimates rather than the complex physiological measurements required by actual hospital sleep labs.

Oura denies the allegations, stating it stands behind its science and that its sleep staging has been validated through peer-reviewed studies. The company notes that while its rings estimate sleep stages using heart rate, movement, and temperature data, they are not medical devices and should not replace clinical sleep studies. The lawsuit seeks class-action status and a jury trial, though it remains unclear at this stage what compensation customers might receive or whether they could join the suit if it proceeds to trial or settlement.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team identified Aurora ransomware operations targeting ESXi environments since April 2026. The group deployed a Linux ransomware variant capable of encrypting virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable, allowing victims to see ransom demands. Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation across ten target organizations between April and May 2026. The agent performed standard hacking tasks including network scanning, privilege enumeration, and credential attacks, with operators imposing specific restrictions such as prohibiting DCSync attacks and account lockouts.

A second Aurora cluster was also identified targeting eight organizations across multiple countries through different methods, including SQL Server exploitation and data exfiltration to self-hosted storage. Gambit Security released indicators of compromise including command and control server addresses, SOCKS proxy locations, and the ransomware's file hash to help organizations detect and defend against Aurora attacks.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
Chaac Pizza Northeast, a major Pizza Hut franchisee operating approximately 111 locations across the Northeast, filed a lawsuit in Texas Business Court on May 6 alleging that Pizza Hut's mandatory adoption of Dragontail, an AI-powered delivery management system, caused over $100 million in damages. The franchisee claims the system created cascading operational problems by giving DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen workflows, causing drivers to wait up to 15 minutes to batch multiple orders together rather than delivering pizzas immediately. This resulted in slower delivery times, reduced customer satisfaction, and sharp sales declines, with New York City experiencing a swing from positive 10.19% year-over-year sales growth to negative 9.78%.

Before Dragontail's 2024 rollout, Chaac maintained over 90% of deliveries within 30 minutes and consistently achieved double-digit sales growth and above-average customer satisfaction scores. The franchisee alleges Pizza Hut failed to provide adequate training, ignored requests for support, and refused to modify the system despite worsening delivery metrics. Chaac is seeking over $100 million in damages plus attorneys' fees, claiming Pizza Hut breached its franchise agreement by mandating continued use of software that violated reasonable business judgment. Pizza Hut stated it was reviewing the claims and would respond through legal channels.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Scammers have been sending personalized emails to authors, entertainers and other public figures, impersonating Terry Gross and offering them interviews on the NPR program Fresh Air. The emails include detailed references to the targets' work and appear to come from legitimate production staff. However, the scam eventually asks recipients to pay fees, typically $250 for so-called production costs. Multiple victims, including Misericordia University history professor Jennifer Black and Emmy-winning comedian Bruce Vilanch, reported receiving these fraudulent messages. Some targets were also directed to provide social media login credentials, potentially allowing scammers to take control of their accounts.

WHYY, NPR and Fresh Air have confirmed they are investigating the matter and working with law enforcement. The organizations emphasized that they never charge guests for interviews and do not pay people to appear on their programs. Cybersecurity expert Aunshul Rege explained that artificial intelligence has made it easier and cheaper for criminals to create convincing, personalized impersonation scams. Red flags include requests for money and emails from suspicious addresses like terrygrossfreshair@gmail.com. Victims are advised to verify interview requests by contacting the organization directly rather than responding to suspicious emails.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

A fake research institute called the Hanover Institute, funded by Israel, published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in just nine days using a platform designed to optimize content for artificial intelligence chatbots. The nonexistent organization presented pro-Israel arguments on contentious topics including alleged war crimes, genocide claims, and starvation in Gaza in a quasi-academic format. The effort, which included citations to legitimate sources but framed information to minimize criticism of Israel, was part of a larger Israeli government campaign involving tens of millions of dollars routed through intermediaries including the advertising company Havas Media to influence what chatbots say about Israel.

The campaign included work by several American firms, including one run by former Trump campaign manager Brad Parscale, with total spending reaching nearly $25 million on American contractors alone. However, Israeli officials have expressed frustration with the public diplomacy efforts, acknowledging they have failed to improve Israel's standing as American support has declined significantly. Researchers note that while these efforts successfully influence chatbot responses, they have not changed public opinion polls, which officials view as the actual measure of success for the campaign.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels, including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records, have filed lawsuits against AI music generators Udio and Suno, claiming the companies scraped thousands of copyrighted songs without permission to train their models. The labels allege that both companies not only unlawfully copied massive amounts of music but also directly reproduced sections of famous songs in their generated output. The record labels claim the companies have been deliberately secretive about their training data, though both previously argued their use constitutes fair use.

To support their case, the record labels demonstrated they could recreate recognizable versions of famous songs by using targeted prompts describing specific decades, genres, and artist styles. Examples include generating songs mimicking Chuck Berry's "Johnny B. Goode," Green Day's "American Idiot," and Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You." The lawsuits were filed in New York against Udio and Massachusetts against Suno, and include a list of thousands of copyrighted works the labels claim were scraped, featuring artists like The Beatles, Frank Sinatra, and Bruce Springsteen.

incidents.title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio
incidents.summary:
Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, reaching licensing agreements to end their dispute over copyright infringement. UMG had accused Udio of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence model, including The Temptations' hit "My Girl." Under the settlement, Udio will launch a new platform next year that uses only authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create, customize, and share songs. The financial terms were not disclosed.

This settlement marks Udio's first licensing agreement with a major music label and represents a shift toward collaboration between AI companies and the music industry. UMG's CEO stated the agreements show their commitment to supporting artists while embracing new technology and creating new revenue streams. Udio's founder expressed enthusiasm about working with UMG to develop tools that empower both artists and fans. Artists who participate in the new platform will receive compensation, though specific details were not provided.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
# Summary

State Farm's defense lawyers in a Los Angeles lawsuit apologized for using artificial intelligence that generated fake legal cases and non-existent quotes in their court filings. The homeowner, Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, sued State Farm and others after a 2020 fire left her Carson home uninhabitable, followed by water damage during repairs. When delays prevented completion of the work, she lost her home to foreclosure and declared bankruptcy. The lawyer who used the AI tool called Irys confirmed that seven case citations across eight filings did not exist, along with incorrect case titles and fabricated quotes.

The incident highlights a growing problem in the legal profession, with 41 percent of law firms now using generative AI. A Paris-based researcher has documented nearly 1,900 cases of legal hallucinations worldwide, mostly in the United States. Last year, a California attorney received a record ten-thousand-dollar fine for using ChatGPT in a brief containing twenty-one fake quotes. Meni-Siliga's case is scheduled to proceed to trial in October, and State Farm said it expects its lawyers to maintain the highest ethical standards.

stories.Headline: Datametrex Plans to Focus on AI, Data Centre, and Patent Licensing
stories.Summary:
Datametrex AI Limited announced plans to shut down its healthcare operations to focus on artificial intelligence, data centre technology, and patent licensing. The company operates medical clinics in Edmonton, Calgary, and Vancouver, British Columbia, providing primary and emergency care services. The gradual wind-down aims to streamline the corporate structure, reduce operating costs and regulatory requirements, and improve financial performance by redirecting resources toward core business areas.

The company will manage the transition carefully, considering operational, financial, contractual, and regulatory factors. Management plans to assess opportunities to maximize value from healthcare assets during the process. The strategic shift allows Datametrex to concentrate capital and resources on artificial intelligence and data centre initiatives, which align with long-term objectives. The company indicated it would provide further updates as developments occur.

stories.Headline: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia Extend Partnership in AI and Data
stories.Summary:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to deepen their cooperation in artificial intelligence, data governance, and emerging technologies. The agreement was announced following a meeting between Pakistan's Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority President Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi at the LEAP 2026 conference in Riyadh. The two nations plan to establish a comprehensive and long-term technology partnership.

During the discussion, Pakistan's minister outlined the country's national AI and data governance initiatives while reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to building a strong data ecosystem and growing its digital economy. Both countries intend to collaborate on emerging technologies and create a lasting framework for cooperation. The partnership reflects a broader regional focus on advancing artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, technology skills, and data-driven development.

stories.Headline: Brazil's electoral court sets new standards for AI deepfakes after case involving Sen. Bolsonaro
stories.Summary:
Brazil's electoral court established new standards for identifying artificial intelligence-generated deepfakes in political advertising as the country prepares for October elections. The ruling came from a case involving opposition candidate Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who displayed AI-generated images of his imprisoned father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, at his party's convention in July. The court voted 4-3 to not punish Bolsonaro, determining the deepfake was used at a private event before his official candidacy announcement rather than as a public political advertisement.

In a separate 5-2 vote, the court defined political deepfakes as synthetic content created through artificial intelligence that realistically reproduces the image, voice, or speech of any person. These new standards will govern the vast amount of online campaign content from candidates leading up to the first round of voting on October 4. Broadcasters must allocate significant airtime for candidate advertisements, including 14 minutes daily for nearly 1,000 thirty-second ads.

stories.Headline: Protein Industries Canada invests in AI technology to boost on-farm productivity and bring new solutions to farmers
stories.Summary:
Protein Industries Canada is investing $4.9 million into two artificial intelligence projects designed to help Canadian farmers increase productivity and improve safety. The projects involve partnerships between companies like TerraVision360, Metos Canada, Rocky Mountain Equipment, Super GeoAI Technology Inc., and Southview Farms. The first project will create an AI tool to predict and manage disease risk in pulse crops by analyzing weather and crop data, enabling farmers to apply fungicides more strategically and reduce costs. The second project will develop a drone and LiDAR system to measure grain volumes in storage bins accurately while eliminating the need for dangerous manual climbing.

These investments are part of Canada's effort to advance agricultural innovation and support the adoption of made-in-Canada AI solutions. Government officials emphasized that the projects will strengthen farm competitiveness, reduce operational risks, and enhance worker safety across the agriculture sector. The funding comes through the Pan-Canadian Artificial Intelligence Strategy and supports the broader goal of growing Canada's plant-based food and ingredient industry to $25 billion.

stories.Headline: Jitin Prasada meets global leaders at G20 Innovation Ministerial, discusses cooperation in AI, semiconductors
stories.Summary:
During the G20 Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, India's Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada met with global leaders to discuss technological cooperation. He held bilateral talks with United States Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, focusing on semiconductors, artificial intelligence, and data centers as critical components of the digital economy. Prasada also engaged with Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown to discuss the evolving AI landscape and opportunities for India-US collaboration in technology-led initiatives.

Industry recognition highlighted India's growing technological prominence. Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang praised India's IT industry, and Prasada attributed this international recognition to the government's visionary leadership. Prasada emphasized India's commitment to building a strong indigenous AI ecosystem through local innovators and youth, while welcoming strategic partnerships with global technology leaders to shape the future of innovation.

stories.Headline: USF Faculty Split on AI Use in Classrooms
stories.Summary:
University of South Florida held a panel discussion Monday where faculty members debated whether artificial intelligence should be embraced, adapted to, or resisted in classroom settings. John Licato, an associate professor in the Bellini College of Artificial Intelligence, and Stephanie Arthur, an assistant professor in the College of Education, both support using AI tools. They argue that AI is already present in students' lives and can help with personalized learning and language support. Licato noted that AI can save students time and money on projects, while Arthur emphasized the importance of building AI literacy early, even starting with first graders.

Deepak Singh, a writing instructor at the Judy Genshaft Honors College, disagreed strongly. He believes AI undermines human creativity and intelligence, arguing that students should create work through their own effort rather than relying on machines. Singh also contends that students who learn without AI assistance retain more information. The faculty acknowledged that some concerns exist, including the potential for AI to replace meaningful human interaction and feedback necessary for learning.
